q: The zone where two ecosystems meet, like a mangrove between land and sea, is called…
x: An ecotone is a transition zone. It often has more species than either side (edge effect).

q: Which of these is NOT one of India's four biodiversity hotspots?
x: India's four hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka and Sundaland (Nicobar).

q: What is the IUCN Red List status of the olive ridley turtle?
x: The olive ridley is Vulnerable. In India it is in Schedule I of the Wildlife Act.

q: Which law is called the umbrella law for the environment in India?
x: It was passed after the Bhopal gas tragedy and gives the Centre wide powers.

q: Which protocol protects the ozone layer?
x: Montreal phases out ozone-depleting gases. Kyoto = greenhouse gases; Cartagena = biosafety; Nagoya = benefit sharing.

q: By which year does India aim to reach net-zero emissions?
x: Announced at COP26 in Glasgow (2021) as part of the Panchamrit.

q: COP30 was held in ___, and COP31 in ___.
x: COP30: Belém, Brazil (2025). COP31: Antalya, Türkiye (November 2026). COP29 was Baku; COP28 Dubai.

q: Where is the head office of the UN Environment Programme (UNEP)?
x: UNEP is in Nairobi, Kenya. The UNFCCC secretariat is in Bonn.

q: The build-up of a poison at higher levels of the food chain is called…
x: Biomagnification: e.g. DDT becomes more concentrated in birds of prey than in the fish they eat.

q: As of October 2026, how many Ramsar sites does India have?
Which country hosted World Environment Day 2025?
x: 2025: Republic of Korea. 2024: Saudi Arabia. 2026: Azerbaijan. 2023: Côte d'Ivoire.

q: Which gas is the main human-made cause of the greenhouse effect?
x: CO₂ contributes the most to human-caused warming, mainly from burning fossil fuels.

q: Which was India's first biosphere reserve?
x: Nilgiri, 1986, across Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.
